summary: PhysicsLabRuntime.new() claims authority for the deterministic permanent lab but only checks schemaVersion, recipeKey, and a non-empty entity array. A caller can therefore supply the canonical recipe key with a forged top-level WorldId/RegionId or a strict subset/substitution of the canonical 20 entities and obtain a valid runtime whose authority no longer corresponds to PhysicsLabRecipe.build(). The production Realizer currently passes PhysicsLabRecipe.build() directly, so this is a source-boundary hardening gap rather than accepted Studio evidence or a current Workspace divergence. Add a narrow fail-closed constructor fence that verifies canonical lab provenance and exactly one canonical key/id pair for the complete recipe population before runtime registration, with pure regressions for provenance mismatch and subset/substitution.
evidence: src/shared/Physics/PhysicsLabRuntime.luau new(recipe) asserts only schemaVersion, recipeKey, and #recipe.entities > 0 before registering every supplied record.
tests/physics_lab_recipe.luau independently locks PhysicsLabRecipe.build() to 20 deterministic entities, required keys, unique StableIds, and entity origins bound to the canonical WorldId/RegionId.
Docs/PHYSICS_LAB.md defines PhysicsLabRecipe as the owner of stable lab/world/entity identity, while merged PR #189 describes PhysicsLabRuntime as registering exactly the current recipe population.
Current production PhysicsLabRealizer.realize() builds the canonical recipe internally, so no Roblox Studio PASS/FAIL inference follows from this source finding.
